summary: Keep a few related actions in one row with shared spacing and modes.

useWhen.text: Keep a few related actions in one row with shared spacing and modes.

from.quote: Keep a few related actions in one row with shared spacing and modes.

anatomy.holds: The group itself: it fills the width its host provides, centres its children vertically, and adds no padding or background.

from.quote: Fills the width its host provides, centers children vertically, and adds no padding or background.

anatomy.holds: A direct IconButton child, which keeps its own circular size instead of stretching.

from.quote: A direct IconButton child keeps its own circular size instead of stretching.

anatomy.holds: One token gap that separates every pair of neighbouring children.

from.quote: One token gap, buttonGroup/gap, separates every pair of neighbors.

anatomy.holds: Button children; every Button stretches, so the Buttons share the remaining width equally.

from.quote: Every Button child stretches, so the Buttons share the remaining width equally.

placementAdvice.text: The host sets the width: ButtonGroup fills the width it receives.

from.quote: ButtonGroup fills the width it receives.
Give the group a width

placementAdvice.text: Do not let the group shrink to its content: without a host width, the Buttons divide the smallest possible row and a label such as “Request” is cut short.

from.quote: Without a host width, the Buttons divide the smallest possible row and “Request” is cut short.

placementAdvice.text: Each IconButton keeps its size and the Buttons divide the rest, so a narrow host can shorten labels.

from.quote: IconButtons keep their size and Buttons divide the rest, so a narrow host can shorten labels.

placementAdvice.text: In the guide's shared-bill example, a Card holds the context and the ButtonGroup keeps split, request and pay together, with Pay emphasized.

from.quote: A Coin Card holds the context. The ButtonGroup keeps split, request, and pay together, with Pay emphasized.

configuration.text: ButtonGroup exposes no layout options: the children you place and the modes you set on the group decide what people see.

from.quote: ButtonGroup exposes no layout options. The children you place and the modes you set on the group decide what people see.

configuration.text: Put an IconButton in the group directly, not inside a wrapper component: a direct IconButton child keeps its intrinsic size, while a wrapper component around it would stretch.

from.quote: A direct `IconButton` child, checked by element type, keeps its intrinsic size; a wrapper component around it would stretch.

configuration.text: Set modes on the group to change every child together, for example smaller controls and stronger fills.

from.quote: Changing the group modes changes every child together: smaller controls and stronger fills.

configuration.text: Set Button / Size once on the group: every child inherits it, so the row keeps one height.

from.quote: Every child inherits Button / Size M, so the row keeps one height.

configuration.text: Do not override one child's Button / Size: the child's own size wins over the group mode and leaves one short, mismatched action.

from.quote: Pay’s own Button / Size S wins over the group mode and leaves one short, mismatched action.

configuration.text: In the guide's narrow host, Button / Size S on the group shrinks every child, so the labels fit again.

from.quote: Button / Size S on the group shrinks every child, so the labels fit again.

configuration.text: Emphasize one action: in the guide, Pay alone sets Emphasis High in its own modes, so the next step is obvious.

from.quote: Only Pay sets Emphasis High, so the next step is obvious.

configuration.text: Do not set Emphasis High on the group: every action then competes for attention.

from.quote: With Emphasis High on the group, all three actions compete for attention.

configuration.text: State belongs to each child: ButtonGroup has no enabled, disabled or selected state of its own, and each child keeps its own disabled, hover and pressed feedback.

from.quote: ButtonGroup has no enabled, disabled, or selected state of its own. Each child keeps its own disabled, hover, and pressed feedback.

rules.text: Give the group its width and modes; let only the key action stand out.

from.quote: Give the group its width and modes; let only the key action stand out.

rules.text: Keep a group to a few actions that belong together.

from.quote: Keep a group to a few actions that belong together.

rules.text: End with the action people are most likely to choose; supporting actions come first.

from.quote: End with the action people are most likely to choose.

rules.text: Use one or two words for each Button label.

from.quote: Use one or two words

rules.text: Button labels stay on one line: when a Button's share is too narrow, the end of the label is cut off with an ellipsis.

from.quote: Button labels stay on one line. When the share is too narrow, the end of the label is cut off with an ellipsis.

states.when: All actions available: every child resolves the group's modes and responds on its own.

from.quote: Every child resolves the group’s modes and responds on its own.

states.when: One child is unavailable (disabled): that Button fades to half opacity and ignores presses, and keeps its share of the row, so the layout does not shift.

from.quote: The disabled Button fades to half opacity and ignores presses. It keeps its share of the row, so the layout does not shift.

accessibility.text: Name every icon action: give each IconButton a task-based accessibilityLabel, such as “Scan QR code”. Without a label, an IconButton is announced by its icon name, such as “Qr Code”.

from.quote: An IconButton without a label is announced by its icon name, such as “Qr Code”. Specify a task-based label, such as “Scan QR code”, for each icon action.

doDont.why: Without a host width, the Buttons divide the smallest possible row and “Request” is cut short.

from.quote: Give the group a width

doDont.do: Set the size once on the group
doDont.why: Pay’s own Button / Size S wins over the group mode and leaves one short, mismatched action.

from.quote: Set the size once on the group

examples.purpose: Split, request and pay in one row: the icon keeps its size, the Buttons share the rest, and only Pay sets a stronger Emphasis.
examples.jsx:
<ButtonGroup
  style={{ width: 360 }}
  modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light', 'Button / Size': 'M', Emphasis: 'Medium', AppearanceBrand: 'Primary' }}
>
  <IconButton iconName="ic_split" accessibilityLabel="Split bill" onPress={() => {}} />
  <Button label="Request" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ AppearanceBrand: 'Secondary' }} />
  <Button label="Pay" onPress={() => {}} modes={{ Emphasis: 'High' }} />
</ButtonGroup>

from.quote: The ButtonGroup keeps split, request, and pay together, with Pay emphasized.

examples.purpose: A narrow host: Button / Size S set once on the group shrinks every child so the labels fit.

from.quote: Button / Size S on the group shrinks every child, so the labels fit again.

props.name: children
props.description: Fragments are flattened. A direct IconButton child, checked by element type, keeps its intrinsic size; every other child (such as Button) gets flex: 1, and a wrapper component around an IconButton would stretch. Declared: Child elements to be rendered inside the button group. Typically generic buttons or icon buttons.

props.name: modes
props.description: Cloned into every child; a child's explicit modes win. The group itself renders a centred row with a 12 px token gap and no padding. Declared: Mode configuration for design tokens (e.g., {"Button / Size": "M", "Emphasis": "High"}) These modes cascade to all children; a child's own `modes` still win on conflict.

slots.description: Child elements to be rendered inside the button group. Typically generic buttons or icon buttons.
